steps.content: July 10, N.F. 116, MBCC Mania Research Lab
Why? What for?
Wynn pores over the Hollow Syndrome case files again and again, but nothing clicks.
Since they returned to the Bureau from Nelson's apartment, no new Hollow Syndrome cases have surfaced in Eastside.
The overwhelming collection of merchandise from Nelson's home has become their last viable lead...
Well, perhaps not quite the last. In one corner of the research lab, a far more ruthless and direct experiment is already in progress.

Inside the specialized containment pod, sealed off from all Mania contamination, Cole—the security team's most courageous volunteer—has willingly confined himself, every safety protocol firmly in place.
On the other side of the transparent door, Eugene stands with a laptop loaded with every piece of Phanuel video content in existence.
Eugene flips open the laptop and hits play.

steps.speaker: Cole
steps.content: Phanuel... Oh, Phanuel, you're singing...
Eugene snaps the laptop shut.

steps.speaker: Cole
steps.content: Huh, Captain?
Eugene flips open the laptop and hits play.

steps.speaker: Cole
steps.content: Hehehe, so cute...
Eugene snaps the laptop shut.

steps.speaker: Cole
steps.content: Huh, Captain?
Clearly, this experiment only confirms one thing:

steps.speaker: Researcher B
steps.content: Look here. After the Mania spike peaks, it doesn't climb further toward mutation, and it doesn't decay either. Instead, it settles into a flat, sustained band.

steps.speaker: Researcher A
steps.content: It's almost like something is deliberately stabilizing the M-value right at the mutation threshold...

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: I've worked cases with Chief for years. I've seen Mania energy absorbed. I've seen it amplified. But deliberately holding an energy field at a specific value, following a pattern, that's a first...

An unnatural stillness hangs over the research lab. From Cole's corner, a dopey giggle surfaces now and then. Apart from that, only the white noise of the air conditioner and the whisper of turning pages. No signs of mutation. No contamination residue. The investigation is stuck, with nowhere to gain purchase.

Wynn sinks her head into the mound of documents in despair. If only Chief were here... Chief would point at some overlooked corner and say, "Something's wrong here," and then everything would just fall into pla—
♪ Ba ba ba ba, ba ba ba ba!
All eyes turn toward the sound and find Eugene holding a plush doll that's shaking violently in his grip.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: Sorry... I'm shutting it off now!
Eugene juggles the thing like a hot potato, flipping it from hand to hand, unable to find a switch anywhere.

steps.speaker: Little Doll
steps.content: Ba ba ba ba! Sorry... I'm shutting it off now! Ba ba ba ba! Sorry... I'm shutting it off now!

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Wait, is that a Phanuel repeating plushie? That's kind of cute, actually.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: What's a repeating plushie?

steps.speaker: Repeating Plushie
steps.content: Ba ba ba ba! Sorry... I'm shutting it off now! Repeating plushie? That's kind of cute, actually... What's a repeating plushie? What's a repeating plushie? What's a repeating—
Crack. The flustered security captain resolves the situation the old-fashioned way, with sheer, brute strength...

Silence returns to the research lab. Eugene, looking somewhat embarrassed, sets the now-headless doll back onto the evidence pile. His eyes drift to the keychain he had been about to study next. After a moment's thought, he sets it back down, still rattled.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: That one's safe. It won't start screaming at you. It's a mini-album.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: An album? That tiny thing?

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: <size=30>Welcome to the future, old man. Albums come in a million formats now. Mini-albums are basically just a tiny USB drive. Then there's the ultra-ultra-ultra VIP limited colored vinyl, regular vinyl, and standard CDs with deluxe editions, standard editions... And depending on the cover, you've got versions A, B, C, and D. Each one comes with different inclusions.</size>

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: Wynn. Please. Stop. Just stop—

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: You know, you were the same way at the scene. You've got this natural immunity to youth culture. Cole and the others got pulled right in. You didn't even flinch.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: I've just never cared much for pop culture. That's all.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Mm-hm. I know. Work is your whole life. "And my captain, Eugene, he drags us all over the city on patrol, and we never catch a single Sinner..."

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: Cole said that when he was under her influence! Y-you heard all of that?

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Heard it? I pulled the footage from his body recorder. It's important case evidence now! That will give Chief solid grounds to bring Phanuel in for questioning.

Wynn's words are perfectly professional, but she makes a point of waving her terminal screen right under Eugene's nose. On it, the full recording of the security captain being utterly shown up by his own subordinate plays on loop.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: Ahem... So if you were there the whole time, how come Phanuel didn't affect you?

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Simple. I already have an idol. And my idol is—
Eugene braces himself, eager and on edge, waiting for Wynn to speak.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: <size=44>Our brilliant, unstoppable, can-do-anything Chief!</size>
Awkwardness has a way of making people fidget. Eugene puts the keychain down, picks it back up, puts it down again... then finally grabs something that looks like a magic wand.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: That's Phanuel's official light stick. Before a concert, the agency usually has the idol do a promo video to push sales. Fans buy them to bring to the show, kind of a badge of honor. Proof you're a loyal fan.
The light stick's design is far more straightforward than that of the doll. Eugene spots the power button immediately and presses it.
[White Flash] [Scene Filter]

A cascade of pink light floods the lab in an instant, drenching every person and every piece of equipment in rosy glow. The hollow heart-and-wing pattern carved along the wand's shaft begins to spin with the light, picking up speed—
Everyone's attention locks onto the light stick, their eyes tracking the spinning wings as they trace left to right, left to right...
[Red Flash] [Horror Sound Effect] [Cole Jumps Out]

steps.speaker: Cole
steps.content: Phanuel... Phanuel... Phanuel...
Cole, who has been sitting silently inside the testing pod this entire time, suddenly stands up and starts murmuring the same words on repeat.
No alarms sound. Cole's M-value simply stabilizes at an extremely high threshold, and then... once, twice, it pulses, ticking up and down in sync with the light stick's rhythm.

steps.speaker: Cole
steps.content: Phanuel... Phanuel... Phanuel...
His hollow, mechanical chanting echoes through the lab, just like a repeating plushie.

Eugene shuts off the light stick at once. The researchers waste no time activating the Hypercube shielding to force Cole's M-value back down. The lab, dead calm just moments ago, now churns with restless anxiety. The same thought crosses every mind:

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: That concert venue seats around thirty thousand people. If every one of them has a light stick...

steps.speaker: Researcher B
steps.content: Based on the victim Nelson's condition alone, if you gather tens of thousands of Hollow Syndrome victims with similarly elevated M-values in one place, you could trigger a Ring-level resonance disaster.

steps.speaker: Repeating Plushie
steps.content: Disaster! Disaster! Disaster! Disaster!
That creepy repeating plushie has somehow turned itself back on.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Chief always says to look past the surface. What if the Hollow Syndrome isn't the real goal...? The security team recovered fast. Eugene and I never even got affected. Maybe Hollow Syndrome isn't the weapon, but a filter...

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: That makes sense. It screens for people who are already susceptible. People who'd want to go to the concert. Who'd buy the light stick for the event. That's the point...
Behind the Hollow Syndrome, there has to be a larger conspiracy, one using the concert as its stage... This lead alone is more than enough to mobilize the Bureau.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: I'll contact Chief!
By the time Cole regains his senses under the Hypercube's suppression, the lab is almost empty. Wynn is already hurrying out, her arms piled high with case files.

steps.speaker: Cole
steps.content: Hey, Wynn! Where are you going?

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Tracking down Nelson's online contacts. Hardcore fans like him have got to know each other. Someone needs to warn them before it's too late!
